sources.fact: The Spring 2026 update is a January 2026 snapshot and separates fixed coverage, FWA, take-up, satellite and mobile evidence.
sources.guard: Do not convert snapshot coverage, take-up or affordability into a current accepted retail order.

sources.fact: The 2026 planned-deployment report uses January 2026 operator plans to end-2028 and defines high confidence using design and committed-funding criteria.
sources.guard: High-confidence planning remains forward-looking and is not proof of live coverage, activation or retail orderability.

sources.fact: Ofcom's PND background covers operator plans, including private and publicly supported deployments, but excludes separate public-authority aspirations.
sources.guard: Keep operator plans distinct from local or national authority aspirations and procurement intentions.

sources.fact: Ofcom publishes fixed coverage, fixed performance and mobile coverage as separate products with different methodologies and granularities.
sources.guard: Do not assign active-line or area performance measures to a target postcode, UPRN or parcel.

sources.fact: USO assessment considers existing service, publicly funded plans within 12 months and build cost before a request can proceed.
sources.guard: USO eligibility or assessment is not evidence of an existing connection or completed build.

sources.fact: The May 2026 NR OMR checks current and planned gigabit infrastructure over three years and runs in January, May and September.
sources.guard: A supplier plan submitted in an OMR window is not a delivery commitment, activation date or accepted order.

sources.fact: The May 2026 OMR closed on 1 June; submissions entered evaluation and postcode/UPRN outputs were to follow after assessment.
sources.guard: Submission receipt or closure is not assessed coverage and must remain pending until published output and matching epoch exist.

sources.fact: The January 2026 consultation records updates to required fields and later links regional outputs from the evaluated review.
sources.guard: Retain the exact output release and required-field version; do not combine supplier returns from different OMR epochs.

sources.fact: BDUK completed evaluation of January submissions and issued classifications for existing and planned qualifying infrastructure.
sources.guard: White, Grey, Black and Under Review are subsidy-control classifications at a point in time, not retail availability states.

sources.fact: The RFI uses AddressBase Premium Epoch 123 UPRN lists and distinguishes voucher project, issued and claimed states.
sources.guard: Preserve UPRN epoch, licence constraints and voucher state; a claimed voucher still requires evidence for target-premise live service.

sources.fact: BDUK's collection separates official delivery statistics, monthly contract reports and annual accounts.
sources.guard: Do not merge management information, official statistics and financial reporting into one premise-level availability measure.

sources.fact: The July report is a 16 July snapshot, covers initial contract scope and warns of variable ingestion lag and non-comparability with official statistics.
sources.guard: Contract-level built counts cannot establish that a selected UPRN is live, orderable or contractually complete.

sources.fact: The June report is a 17 June management-information snapshot and distinguishes contract delivery counts from subsidy-attributable official statistics.
sources.guard: A monthly count change may reflect reporting timing and cannot be projected to an address without matching premise evidence.

sources.fact: The April report excludes deferred-scope premises and says ingestion lag makes the figures unsuitable for assessing contractual milestones.
sources.guard: Do not interpret missing deferred scope or lagged records as NO_DATA, failure or completion for a target premise.

sources.fact: OS Places defines Find, Postcode and UPRN capture requests separately from Nearest, BBOX, Radius and Polygon GeoSearch requests.
sources.guard: A spatial candidate search must not be promoted to an exact address or UPRN match.

sources.fact: The BBOX request is limited to one square kilometre and documents coordinate precision and classification/lifecycle filters.
sources.guard: Split larger areas deterministically and retain filters, CRS and paging; a BBOX hit is not parcel containment.

sources.fact: Nearest searches up to 1,000 metres and returns dataset, epoch, last-update and output-CRS metadata.
sources.guard: Retain distance and dataset metadata; proximity cannot transfer broadband evidence between neighbouring units.

sources.fact: OS Features paging uses server-generated previous/next URIs and caps a page at 100 features.
sources.guard: Follow pages to a terminal response; truncation or a missing page is a technical incomplete result, not NO_DATA.

sources.fact: The Buildings theme contains Building, Building Access Location, Building Line and Building Part; OSID is primary and TOID is optional.
sources.guard: Do not treat a building, access point, line and building part as interchangeable or infer absence from a missing TOID.

sources.fact: Building data includes Building-Part and UPRN cross-reference tables with identifiers and version dates.
sources.guard: One building may map to multiple parts and addressable UPRNs; retain relationship and version evidence.

sources.fact: Building Part schema includes under-construction status, version dates and an optional TOID.
sources.guard: Under-construction and superseded versions must be held from current unit or serviceability assertions.

sources.fact: The licensed lookup links mandatory Title_No and UPRN fields and documents limitations from address searching, ingest and matching.
sources.guard: A title-UPRN association requires licensed source, match-quality review and multiplicity handling before parcel binding.

sources.fact: Title Descriptor carries estate interest, class, registration status and change indicator; pending applications may lack estate or class information.
sources.guard: Missing estate/class on an in-progress registration is not NO_DATA and must not be treated as completed title evidence.

sources.fact: HMLR search covers registered property and supports postcode, street/town, map or title-number routes; unregistered land may return no result.
sources.guard: A failed address search is not proof of no land or no title; use map/index-map routes and preserve registered-only scope.

sources.fact: NSUL and ONSUD allocate UPRNs to statistical and administrative geographies using point-in-polygon methods and are released every six weeks.
sources.guard: These are geography lookups used with AddressBase, not address, parcel, ownership or broadband products.

sources.fact: ONS confirms UPRN products are not address products and only publish postcode attributes that pass Code-Point Open licensing checks, with source currency stated by release.
sources.guard: Postcode absence may reflect open-licence filtering or epoch lag; it is not proof that the property or address is absent.
